decisive_items: intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with marked papillary dermal edema, necrosis of vessel walls, and focal fibrinoid necrosis
multiple discrete, round, dry ulcers, most with central eschars, dusky gray borders, and collarettes of scale
response.rationale: Second-biopsy histopathology is diagnostic of leukocytoclastic vasculitis: perivascular neutrophils, vessel-wall necrosis, fibrinoid necrosis, and papillary dermal edema. Clinical ulcers/eschars plus high MPO-ANCA and methimazole exposure favor ANCA-associated/drug-induced small-vessel vasculitis. Other candidates lack matching granulomatous, medium-vessel, panniculitic, or SLE-specific features.

rejected.why: No granulomatous inflammation or ENT/pulmonary/renal involvement; p-ANCA is borderline and MPO positivity does not specifically define Wegener granulomatosis.
Biopsy shows dermal small-vessel vasculitis rather than medium-vessel arteritis; no systemic PAN features and ANCA is not typical for PAN.
Only low-titer ANA and anti-SSA/Ro with normal complements and absent SLE criteria; high MPO-ANCA favors ANCA-associated vasculitis.
Same histologic evidence as R4 but less specific; the leukocytoclastic subtype is directly supported by the biopsy.
Erythema induratum is primarily a lobular panniculitis usually associated with TB; biopsy shows dermal small-vessel vasculitis without lobular panniculitis and no TB evidence.
